_why: Iron Rule 2. ONE definition. It is compiled in exactly two places - tools/forbidden-source-names.mjs (JS/TS) and tools/forbidden_source_names.py (Python) - which build a byte-identical pattern; every check imports one of them. tools/audit/forbidden-names-selftest.mjs proves the twins agree and that every probe below is classified correctly. Hand-compiling these names elsewhere is how four copies drifted into four behaviours by 2026-09-24, and only one of them caught 'R.K. Bali'.
_scope: The rule targets ATTRIBUTION - presenting someone else's book as the source of this site's teaching. Capt. Pahil ruled 2026-08-02 that the bare word is not banned ('oxford is a name, city, street, university'). So these patterns are deliberately multi-word and specific: 'Oxford Aviation', never 'Oxford'.
_plain: Names must be letters and digits, separated by single spaces or hyphens. The compilers refuse anything else.
_matching: Case-insensitive. A token of 2-3 capital letters is read as initials: spaces or dots may sit between its letters and one dot may follow, so 'RK Bali' catches 'R.K. Bali', 'R. K. Bali', 'R.K.Bali' and 'RK-Bali'. Tokens are joined by any run of spaces, dots or hyphens. The match must START at a word boundary ('work Bali', 'basic Joshi' do not match) but need not end at one ('Oxford textbook' does). Initials were first added to the scrubber alone on 2026-09-19; the other copies stayed exact until 2026-09-24.

probes._note: Calibration table, run by tools/audit/forbidden-names-selftest.mjs against BOTH compilers. Add a line here whenever a spelling slips past, or a harmless sentence is wrongly caught.
probes._known_gaps: Attribution these patterns do NOT catch, listed so nobody assumes they do. Surname-first citations are not matched. Raw HTML must be reduced to visible text (tags stripped, entities decoded) before it is checked - the self-test reports these, it does not fail on them.
